answer_text:
For a smooth function \(b(x)\) with simple zeros \(x_i\),

\[
\delta(b(x))=\sum_i \frac{\delta(x-x_i)}{|b'(x_i)|}.
\]

Here

\[
b(x)=\sin(\pi x),
\]

whose zeros on \([0,\infty)\) are

\[
x_i=n,\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots
\]

and

\[
b'(x)=\pi\cos(\pi x)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|b'(n)|=\pi|\cos(\pi n)|=\pi.
\]

Thus, on the integration interval,

\[
\delta(\sin(\pi x))
=
\frac{1}{\pi}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\delta(x-n).
\]

Therefore,

\[
I
=
\int_{0}^{\infty}
\delta(\sin(\pi x))\,2^{-x}\,dx
=
\frac{1}{\pi}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}2^{-n}.
\]

The geometric series gives

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}2^{-n}
=
\frac{1}{1-\frac12}
=
2.
\]

Hence, under the standard convention that the Dirac mass at the lower endpoint \(x=0\) is included fully,

\[
I=\frac{2}{\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{2}{\pi}}
\]

Remark: If a different endpoint convention is used for the delta at \(x=0\) (for example, half-weight or exclusion), the value changes; the calculation above uses the common full-inclusion convention for the endpoint atom.
